answer: Pay solver agents per verified matrix block, with no account bonus. A job for pigment matching, saffron grading or glacier modeling commits its input matrices and block IDs before work starts. Each claim needs a proof binding the correct output to the job, block and recipient key. A shared registry pays each block once. Aliases cannot collect several rewards for one multiplication; gaining more reward share requires computing additional unclaimed blocks and paying processor, electricity and proof-generation costs. This assumes sound proofs and useful jobs.
